personas.name: routine-diagnose-hypertension-stage1-complete
personas.description: Well-formed routine GP referral: raised clinic BP confirming a new hypertension diagnosis, 24-hour ABPM requested (NICE NG136 first-line confirmation), no oscillometric accuracy concerns, every completeness field present — expect usually-appropriate + ok + routine + accept.

request.clinicalQuestion: Clinic BP 148/94 on two separate occasions — confirm or exclude a diagnosis of hypertension before starting treatment.
request.relevantHistory: No previous cardiovascular history. Family history of hypertension.

triage.notes: Monitor to be fitted and returned to the practice nurse.

firedRules.description: Clinic BP >=140/90 confirming a new diagnosis — ABPM is the recommended confirmation method (NICE NG136).
No oscillometric accuracy factors identified — standard ABPM is suitable.
No escalation triggers; triage follows the requested urgency (routine).

personas.name: white-coat-hypertension-atrial-fibrillation-limited-redirect
personas.description: Suspected white-coat hypertension with markedly variable clinic readings: out-of-office monitoring is usually appropriate for this indication, but the patient has known atrial fibrillation, which reduces oscillometric ABPM accuracy — suitability is 'limited' and the recommendation redirects to an auscultatory alternative regardless of how appropriate the test choice was — expect usually-appropriate + limited + routine + redirect.

request.clinicalQuestion: Clinic BP consistently elevated (155-170/95-100) but home readings normal — confirm suspected white-coat effect before starting treatment.
request.relevantHistory: Known paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, rate-controlled on bisoprolol. Anxious during clinic appointments.

triage.notes: Consider manual auscultatory home readings given the AF.

firedRules.description: Suspected white coat hypertension — out-of-office monitoring is usually appropriate (NICE NG136).
Atrial fibrillation reduces the accuracy of oscillometric ABPM (BIHS) — consider auscultatory confirmation.
No escalation triggers; triage follows the requested urgency (routine).

flags.description: Atrial fibrillation reduces oscillometric ABPM accuracy (BIHS).
flags.suggestedAction: Use an AF-validated device or confirm readings auscultatorily; interpret ABPM results with caution.

personas.name: urgent-severe-hypertension-priority-review-incomplete
personas.description: Clinic BP well into the severe/accelerated range: NICE NG136 makes same-day specialist review the priority over routine ABPM confirmation, so appropriateness is only may-be-appropriate (score 4) even though the request itself is otherwise reasonable, and the severe reading independently forces urgent triage; several administrative fields are not yet captured — expect may-be-appropriate + ok + urgent + accept, completeness below 100.

request.clinicalQuestion: Clinic BP 190/125 today, asymptomatic — same-day same-day BP recheck and target-organ-damage screen arranged; ABPM requested to characterise variability once stable.
request.relevantHistory: No previous hypertension diagnosis. No headache, chest pain, or visual disturbance today.

triage.notes: Same-day specialist review arranged separately per NICE NG136; ABPM to follow once acute review complete.
